dossier.valuation_method: Probability-weighted, time-discounted scenario rNPV (real option on MST reaching volume-production royalties). Probabilities built BOTTOM-UP from per-program HVM base rates (~5-15% literature, adjusted) aggregated via 1-prod(1-p); success-branch economics DERIVED from IP-licensor margins (~60% net) and exit multiples (18-22x, vs Rambus/InterDigital/CEVA/Arm); 15% systematic+illiquidity discount rate; cross-checked vs net-cash floor and EV/sales.
dossier.thesis_summary: Atomera is a pre-revenue semiconductor materials-IP licensor whose entire value is an option on Mears Silicon Technology (MST) reaching volume-production royalties. The physics is real and published, but MST is a 'nice-to-have' (every job it does has a mature production incumbent), which is why it produced ~$65k of revenue and ~$242M of cumulative losses in a decade and just lost its flagship ST royalty path. Valued as a probability-weighted real option with bottom-up per-program success rates, FMV is ~$2.65/share (band $1.75-$4.80) over a ~$1.00 net-cash floor; the expected value is driven by ~18%-probability high-value GAA/DRAM/power adoption branches, not the ~64%-likely failure outcome.
key_value_drivers: Probability of >=1 high-value HVM adoption (GAA/DRAM/power) - modeled ~18% bottom-up, base-rate-low ~10%
Undisclosed per-wafer royalty rate / per-fab magnitude ($6M-$72M/fab/yr at $20-$120/wafer)
Number and breadth of design wins (GAA, DRAM, RF-SOI, power, GaN - multiple independent shots on goal)
Timing to first material royalty and dilution before inflection (~48-52M shares at maturity)
Maturity royalty margin (~60% net) and exit multiple (18-22x) per IP-licensor comps
key_risks: Structural 'nice-to-have': no customer is forced to adopt; mature incumbents are good-enough (~64% failure weight)
Continuous dilution (~$18M/yr burn, ~$40M undrawn ATM) at depressed prices until a deal closes
Performance/reliability (HCI) tradeoffs recur in power; ST walked away after full integration
Single-source/vendor-reported data on newest GAA and GaN claims; not independently validated at scale
Securities-law investigation overhang (May 2026); binary, lumpy, concentrated outcomes
what_would_change_my_mind: A signed HVM/royalty license with a named foundry/IDM/memory maker
Independent peer-reviewed confirmation of 2nm GAA diffusion-blocking superiority or GaN parasitic-channel result
Disclosure/inference of a royalty rate at the high end of the band or a multi-fab license structure
A second Tier-1 walk-away or failed GAA evaluation (downside)
A discounted emergency capital raise extending the timeline further (downside)
